verdict.rationale: cubic runs event-triggered agents: it automatically reviews every new PR, re-reviews after force-pushes, and keeps an exported wiki current through a rolling pull request. Fixing is still human-initiated, either one click on 'Fix with cubic' or a comment command, so it does not autonomously fix software on its own trigger. Codebase scans deploy agents to find bugs, but no recurring schedule is documented. Missing for 10: scheduled/cron-based recurring agent runs, autonomous fix-without-human-trigger, general-purpose always-on maintenance agents beyond PR review, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
keeps them current through a rolling pull request
cubic generates the fix and pushes it to your PR branch.
Codebase scans deploy thousands of AI agents to find bugs and vulnerabilities across your repository.
cubic now reviews the new changes after a force-push when it can safely compare them with a previously reviewed version.
